cost_ranges.note: One battery = 10 kWh of capacity. Built only from the published Verbraucherzentrale NRW storage averages (Stand 3 Nov 2026; n = 70 battery offers, Jan 2025 - Aug 2026, installed together with PV): likely = the >8-10 kWh band, EUR 410/kWh x 10 kWh = EUR 4,100; low = the cheapest band, >12-16 kWh at EUR 360/kWh x 10 = EUR 3,600; high = the dearest band, 4-6 kWh at EUR 510/kWh x 10 = EUR 5,100. The page does not state the VAT basis for storage; storage carries 0% VAT (public.vat_rates), so tax-inclusive and ex-tax are the same here. Not a quote.

Built only from the published Verbraucherzentrale NRW size-band AVERAGES for PV up to 10 kWp (Stand 3 Nov 2026; offers Jan 2025 - Aug 2026; n = 71 PV offers over all sizes): low = the >9-10 kWp band, EUR 1,410/kWp; high = the 4-6 kWp band, EUR 2,090/kWp; likely = the unweighted mean of the four published band averages up to 10 kWp (2,090 + 1,820 + 1,520 + 1,410) / 4 = EUR 1,710/kWp (a derived figure: the page gives no per-band counts or medians). Larger systems cost less per kWp. Excludes battery. Prices are net; PV carries 0% VAT (public.vat_rates). Not a quote.
cost_ranges.unit: EUR per watt DC (Verbraucherzentrale EUR per kWp / 1,000)

export_policy_rates.note: 7,70 ct/kWh Teileinspeisung bis 10 kW, Inbetriebnahme 1.8.-31.12.2026 (section 21 i.V.m. sections 48, 49, 53 EEG 2023), Bundesnetzagentur. Held flat over the 20-year payment term.

export_policies.name: EEG-Einspeisevergütung: Überschusseinspeisung (Teileinspeisung), bis 10 kW
export_policies.note: Eigenverbrauch zuerst, der Überschuss wird nach EEG vergütet. Gilt für Anlagen, die vom 1. August bis 31. Dezember 2026 in Betrieb gehen, 20 Jahre lang (section 25 EEG). Ohne intelligentes Messsystem (Smart Meter) muss neue Anlagen die Einspeiseleistung auf 60 Prozent der installierten Leistung begrenzen (section 9 Abs. 2 EEG); dieser Ertragsverlust und der Wegfall der Vergütung bei negativen Strompreisen sind in der Rechnung NICHT berücksichtigt.

export_policy_rates.note: 12,22 ct/kWh Volleinspeisung bis 10 kW, Inbetriebnahme 1.8.-31.12.2026, Bundesnetzagentur. Held flat over the 20-year payment term.

export_policies.name: EEG-Einspeisevergütung: Volleinspeisung, bis 10 kW
export_policies.note: Der gesamte Solarstrom wird eingespeist und zum höheren Volleinspeisesatz vergütet; Ihren Strom kaufen Sie weiter zum normalen Preis, die Stromrechnung sinkt nicht. Gilt für Anlagen, die vom 1. August bis 31. Dezember 2026 in Betrieb gehen, 20 Jahre lang (section 25 EEG). Die Begrenzung auf 60 Prozent ohne Smart Meter und der Wegfall der Vergütung bei negativen Preisen sind NICHT berücksichtigt.

markets.display_round_rationale: Assumption: round money to the nearest EUR 50 so that small homes (savings of a few hundred euros a year) are not rounded to the nearest EUR 100.
markets.name: Germany
markets.vat_note: VAT on installed PV and storage is 0% for private homes up to 30 kWp (section 12(3) UStG), no end date in the statute: see public.vat_rates. markets.vat_rate stays null on purpose (the calculator uses the date-effective table).

model_assumptions.rationale: Product choice: a 20-year projection with no discounting, equal to the EEG payment term (section 25 EEG: 20 years). There is no sourced export price for years 21 to 25, so the model stops where the sourced rate stops. Inverter and battery replacement are not modelled.
Product choice: electricity prices flat (low), rising 2% a year (likely) or 4% a year (high). Not a forecast and not sourced; the same planning range as the GB calculator.

Product choice: one battery is modelled as 10 kWh of capacity, the Verbraucherzentrale NRW storage band >8-10 kWh used for the cost row. The study states capacity, not usable energy. Not a recommendation.

Product choice: install dates are offered only up to 31 Dec 2026, the last day of the sourced EEG feed-in rates (Bundesnetzagentur). The successor rule (EEG-Novelle 2027, Drs. 21/7867) had not passed on 2026-11-22, so no 2027 rate exists to use; the calculator does not guess one. Move this date when the law is passed and rates are sourced.
Input sanity limit for the monthly bill field, so a typing slip (an extra zero) is caught. Not sourced.
Product choice: below this a payback figure is not meaningful for a rooftop installation, so the calculator warns instead. Not sourced.
Product choice: where a source gives a likely value but no bounds, low and high are likely -/+ 15% and the result says they are estimated. Placeholder until bounds are sourced. Same as GB.

Derived from 12 PVGIS 5.3 runs (1 kWp, 35 degree tilt, 14% losses, PVGIS-SARAH3), retrieved 2026-11-22, for Hamburg, Berlin and Muenchen: yield facing east, west or north divided by yield facing south (aspect 0). East/west ratios: Hamburg 0.799 / 0.783, Berlin 0.795 / 0.772, Muenchen 0.784 / 0.782 (low = smallest, high = largest, likely = mean of the six = 0.786). North: 0.520, 0.509, 0.512 (likely = mean = 0.514). Source: https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/api/v5_3/PVcalc (lat/lon of each city, peakpower=1, loss=14, angle=35, aspect=0/90/-90/180).
Product choice: 0.5% less output each year, a conventional planning figure for crystalline silicon panels (same as the GB calculator). Not sourced.

PVGIS system losses (the key keeps its legacy name). 14% is the PVGIS default system loss and what every yield figure on the site uses; 20% (some shade) and 30% (heavy shade) are product choices that step the loss up for partial and heavy shade. Not sourced.

NO PRIMARY SOURCE FOUND (an open item for the owner: a missing fact, not a null column, so the generated docs/TODO-VERIFY.md does not list it). The same deliberately wide product-choice ranges as the GB calculator: how much solar output is used at home rather than exported depends on when the household is at home. Replace with a measured source (for example the HTW Berlin Stromspeicher-Inspektion or a national study) when one is verified.
model_assumptions.unit: fraction of solar output used at home

model_assumptions.rationale: Product choice: the Verbraucherzentrale NRW cost data used for pricing is shown per size band, and the EEG rates used here are those for systems up to 10 kW, so the suggested size is capped at 10 kW rather than priced outside the data. Not sourced.
Product choice: size the system to cover 80% to 100% of estimated annual usage, which gives the low and high ends of the suggested size range. Not sourced.
